doc.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013

title: Closing compliments and thanks
summary: Rowe relays a student's praise of Gardner's playing and the two wrap up.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: You know, we’ve got to get you to your thing. But this has really been fascinating. And one of the best kinds of compliments a person gets is somebody that wasn’t drawn out. One of my saxophone students, Brett, who played with you on the jam session last night, and he said “I really liked that guy. He didn’t play a gazillion notes like some of the other people, and every note seemed to mean something.” He said that about you.
I think that’s a high compliment because he’s a person who listens to a lot of music in addition to playing himself.
Sure. Wow. Okay. I’ll have to send him his check.
Well it’s really been nice talking to you. I look forward to hearing you tonight with the band.
Oh sure thing. Thank you. And it’s a wonderful interview, and I’m glad to be part of it.
Thank you. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-
